div.p: Six-transmembrane epithelial antigen of prostate 3 (STEAP3), a member of the iron regulation protein family, is characterized by a high recurrence rate and a short survival time. Nevertheless, studies investigating the role of STEAP3 in glioblastoma (GB) are scarce. In this study, the prognostic value of STEAP3 was evaluated utilizing mRNA expression profiles from Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) and The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) databases as the validation and training cohorts, respectively. Moreover, differentially expressed genes were subjected to a functional enrichment analysis. The relationship between STEAP3 and the tumor microenvironment (TME) was examined. The immunophenoscore (IPS) and tumor immune dysfunction and exclusion (TIDE) score were used to investigate response to immunotherapy. In all cohorts, GB patients with higher STEAP3 expression levels exhibited shorter overall survival (OS). Additionally, STEAP3-associated genes were primarily implicated in leukocyte migration, the JAK-STAT signaling pathway, and the cytokine-mediated signaling pathway. In the STEAP3 high-expression group, the ESTIMATEScore, ImmuneScore, StromalScore, and IPS were significantly higher. Overall, our results highlighted that STEAP3 might serve as a candidate prognostic biomarker for GB. Additionally, it might regulate the TME and influence GB metastasis.
external cohorts (GSE108474) were used. Additionally, ESTIMATE, CIBERSORT, and GEPIA algorithms were applied to analyze the correlations between the TME and STEAP3.

div.head: Data collection and figure generation
div.p: e mRNA expression patterns and clinical characteristics of individuals with glioma were acquired from the UCSC website (https://xenabrowser.net/)(accessed on January 10, 2024). e training set comprised the RNA-seq data of 668 glioma patients who underwent screening from TCGA GBMLGG Tumors (including 702 samples). Indeterminate or unclassified clinical information was excluded from this study. Based on the GPL570 platform, the GSE108474 (including 479 tumor samples) gene microarray dataset was downloaded on April 10, 2024, from the GEO database at https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/ and served as the external validation set. As the Table 2 showing, we downloaded and conducted a validation analysis, incorporating age, sex, grade, subtype, and glioma-CpG island methylator phenotype (CIMP) status. During survival time and variate analyses, indeterminate or unclassified clinical information was excluded from this study. Tables 1 and 2 list the clinicopathological features and demographics of patients, whilst Table 3 summarizes the tumor abbreviations from TCGA data.

div.head: STEAP3's roles and expression in Pan-cancer
div.p: e Cancer Single-Cell State Atlas (http://cancerSEA.biu.edu.cn) is a newly developed database dedicated to decoding 14 different functional states of 25 types of tumors at the single-cell level (accessed on January 15, 2024) 15,16 . is database contains information on STEAP3 functions in various cancer types. To examine variations in STEAP3 expression between human cancer samples and paired healthy tissues, the Tumor Immune Estimation Resource (TIMER) (https://cistrome.shinyapps.io/timer/, accessed on January 15, 2024) was used, which enabled a methodical examination of immune cell infiltration levels across 10,897 cancer specimens from 32 distinct cancer types.

div.head: Assessment of immunological checkpoints, immunological cell infiltration, and response to immune therapy
div.p: e ESTIMATE package in R (version 1.0.13; http://www.sangerbox.com) (accessed on March 12, 2024) and the ESTIMATE method were used to calculate the StromalScore, ImmuneScore, and ESTIMATEScore of each tumor tissue in the TCGA dataset. Next, the relationships between STEAP3 and ImmuneScore, StromalScore, and ESTIMATEScore were analyzed. Expression spectra were analyzed using the CIBERSORT tool ( h t t p : / / w w w . s a n g e r b o x . c o m ) to identify the proportion of 22 immunological cell types in each tumor specimen. Using data from TCGA GB Tumors, the GEPIA (Gene Expression Profiling Interactive Analysis) ( h t t p : / / g e p i a . c a n c e r -p k u . c n / , obtained by March 16, 2024) offers customized functionalities. Using a scatter plot, the relationships between T cell fatigue markers and STEAP3 were displayed 28 .

To determine response to immune checkpoint blockade therapy targeting PD-L1, PD-1, and CTLA4, the TIDE score was computed using the TIDE algorithm (http://tide.dfci.harvard.edu/, viewed on 16 March 2024) 30 .

div.head: Association between STEAP3 and pan-cancer and expression in GB
div.p: According to the results of the GEPIA database analysis, in addition to GB, STEAP3 mRNA expression levels were significantly higher in several additional forms of cancer compared to adjacent healthy tissues, including COAD (Colon adenocarcinoma), CESC (Cervical squamous cell carcinoma and endocervical adenocarcinoma), LUAD (Lung adenocarcinoma), LUSC (Lung squamous cell carcinoma), OV (Ovarian serous cystadenocarcinoma), THYM ( ymoma), DLBC (Lymphoid Neoplasm Diffuse Large B-cell Lymphoma), UCEC (Uterine Corpus Endometrial Carcinoma), READ(Rectum adenocarcinoma), and UCS (Uterine Carcinosarcoma) (Fig. 1A, B). Likewise, STEAP3 mRNA levels were significantly higher in GB tissues compared to healthy samples from both TCGA cohorts (STEAP3 expression log 2 (TPM + 1), p < 0.01) and the GSE108474 cohort (STEAP3 expression (log2), p < 0.0001; Fig. 2A, B). KM analysis from the TCGA dataset revealed that glioma patients with higher STEAP3 expression levels had shorter overall survival times (HR = 8.25, p < 0.001; Fig. 2C). Importantly, KM survival curve analysis in the validation dataset GSE108474 unveiled that glioma patients with higher STEAP3 expression levels had a shorter OS (HR = 3.91, p < 0.001; Fig. 2D). According to the HPA database, STEAP3 expression levels were higher in glioma tissues compared to normal cerebral cortical organs at both the protein and RNA levels. e top three normal organs with high STEAP3 protein expression included hippocampus, thyroid gland and liver.

e top three normal organs with high STEAP3 RNA expression included liver, parathyroid gland and salivary gland. e top three pathological tissues with high STEAP3 protein expression included prostate cancer, breast cancer and urothelial cancer. e top three pathological tissues with high STEAP3 RNA expression included glioma, liver cancer and lung cancer. (Fig. 3A-D).

div.head: Prognostic utility of STEAP3 in GB
div.p: Patients in the STEAP3 high-expression group had shorter overall survival outcomes, according to stratification studies of the clinical characteristics. We performed stratified analysis from the bilateral levels of TCGA-LGG and TCGA-GBM and confirmed that patients with high STEAP3 expression at the above two levels had a poor prognosis with statistical significance. e GSE108474 external dataset also confirmed the significant predictive significance of STEAP3 at both levels. (Fig. 4A-D, p < 0.01). In addition, the area under the curve (AUC) for predicting one-, three-, and five-year survival rates were 0.87, 0.90, and 0.87, respectively (Fig. 4E). Given that the AUC area is greater than 0.85, the prediction performance is very good. e aforementioned results indicated that STEAP3 could serve as a predictive biomarker for the prognosis of glioma patients. e results further demonstrated that STEAP3 might accurately predict prognosis in high-grade (GB) patients (1-year AUC = 0.63, 3-year AUC = 0.69, 4-year AUC = 0.88) and low-grade glioma (LGG) patients (1-year AUC = 0.87, 3-year AUC = 0.83, 5-year AUC = 0.77) (Fig. 4F, G). ese results were consistent with those in the validation dataset GSE108474. In the high-grade subgroup, patient prognosis was poor due to the elevated STEAP3 expression level. As anticipated, the predictive value of STEAP3 was corroborated by the time-dependent ROC curve for glioma (1-year AUC = 0.72, 3-year AUC = 0.81, and 5-year AUC = 0.81) and for high-grade glioma (GB) ( (1-year AUC = 0.63, 3-year AUC = 0.69, 4-year AUC = 0.88) and low-grade glioma (LGG) patients (1year AUC = 0.73, 3-year AUC = 0.81, 5-year AUC = 0.77) (Fig. 4H-J).

Besides, patients with TCGA-Proneural and TCGA-Classical GB and higher STEAP3 expression levels had poorer survival rates (Fig. 5A-C). e P values of the above two groups were less than 0.05, indicating that the prognosis of the two GB subtypes was highly significantly correlated with the expression of STEAP3. However, in TCGA-Mesenchymal group, p < 0.5, although not as significant as the above two groups, it also indicated that high expression of STEAP3 affected the prognosis of patients. Likewise, Proneural and Classical GB patients with high STEAP3 expression levels in the GSE108474 cohort had poor overall survival outcomes (p < 0.05), but in Mesenchymal group, p > 0.5. As a validation set, these results confirm the reliability of the above conclusions. ( Fig. 5D-F) In addition, univariate and multivariate Cox regression analyses were conducted to assess the potential of STEAP3 as an independent predictor of survival in GB patients. Univariate Cox regression analysis of seven independent variables in TCGA-GBMLGG cohort was carried out. Age, grade, IDH status, 1p/19q co-deletion, MGMT, and STEAP3 expression level, demonstrated a significant prognostic impact on OS. Multivariate Cox regression analysis exhibited that age (HR = 1.040; 95% CI [1.030-1.060]; p < 0.001), grade (HR = 3.580; 95% CI [2.030-6.310]; P < 0.001), IDH status (HR = 2.350; 95% CI [1.450-3.810]; p < 0.001), 1p/19q codeletion (HR = 2.100; 95% CI [1.250-3.510]; p = 0.005), and STEAP3 expression level (HR = 1.010; 95% CI [1.000- 1.030]; p = 0.026) were independent prognostic factors for glioma patients. In that case, STEAP3 was identified as a prognostic predictor for glioma in the univariate Cox regression analysis. Similarly, the Multivariate Cox regression analysis identified STEAP3 as an independent prognostic predictor for glioma in the TCGA (Table 4). In GSE108474 validate cohort, Univariate Cox regression analysis showed that STEAP3 expression level also demonstrated a significant prognostic impact on OS. Multivariate Cox regression analysis indicated that STEAP3 expression level (HR = 1.270; 95% CI [1.010-1.590]; P = 0.04) was independent prognostic factor for glioma patients (Table 5). ese results suggest that higher STEAP3 expression was associated with worse prognosis.

According to the CancerSEA single-cell database, this chart illustrated that STEAP3 was positively correlated with EMT (r = 0.29, p<0.001), invasion (r = 0.26, p<0.001), metastasis (r = 0.26, p<0.001), hypoxia (r = 0.26, p<0.001) and angiogenesis (r = 0.23, p<0.001) in GB (Fig. 6), which might be associated with poor overall survival for GB patients.

div.head: Functional enrichment analysis of STEAP3
div.p: DEG analysis between the high-expression and low-expression groups yielded a total of 1454 DEGS (Fig. 7A, B). In order to elucidate the fundamental biological processes and activities linked to STEAP3, KEGG pathway analysis and GO enrichment analysis of DEGs were carried out. e top 10 significant GO (BP, CC, MF) terms were ranked by ascending FDR. Remarkably, the results demonstrated that the aforementioned DEGs were markedly enriched in numerous TME-associated biological processes, such as leukocyte migration, collagencontaining extracellular matrix, cytokine-mediated signaling pathway, and receptor-ligand activity ( p < 0.001, Fig. 7C-E). At the same time, KEGG analysis exposed significant enrichment in TME-related pathways, including the TNF signaling pathway, JAK-STAT signaling pathway, and cytokine-cytokine receptor interaction (Fig. 7F).

div.head: Immunological infiltration analysis
div.p: e ESTIMATE method showed the associations between immune infiltration scores and STEAP3 expression (log 2 [x + 0.001]). As depicted in Fig. 8A, significant differences were noted (p < 0.0001) in the StromalScore, ImmuneScore, and ESTIMATEScore between the high-expression and low-expression groups. Besides, the immune landscape results between the high-and low-expression groups showed that the STEAP3 highexpression group had relatively higher proportions of neutrophils, monocytes, activated dendritic cells, and regulatory T cells (Tregs) compared to the STEAP3 low-expression group, whereas the STEAP3 high-expression group had lower infiltration levels of follicular helper T cells (Fig. 8B).

div.head: Assessments of immunological checkpoints and response to immune therapy
div.p: Furthermore, the relationship between STEAP3 expression and immunological checkpoints was explored using the GEPIA database. e findings revealed a positive association between STEAP3 expression and granzyme B (GZMB), cytotoxic T lymphocyte-associated antigen-4 (CTLA4), as well as programmed cell death protein 1 (PDCD1; PD-1) ligand 1 (CD274; PDL1) (p < 0.001; Fig. 9A-D). while CD274 displayed the highest correlation coefficient (R = 0.51, p < 0.001).

Following this, the relationship between immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) and STEAP3 expression was examined. We predicted anti-PD1 and anti-CTLA4 immunotherapy response through the TIDE algorithm in GB patients. No significant correlations were found between the TIDE score and STEAP3 levels. Although the results were not statistically significant, the STEAP3 high expression group has shown a trend of high TIDE score, which has certain reference value for evaluating the worse treatment effect and prognosis of patients (p = 0.32; Fig. 9E). Patients with high STEAP3 expression levels had higher IPS for anti-PD-1 and anti-CTLA4 immunotherapies, in particular, IPS-CTLA4(-)/PD-1(+) and IPS-CTLA4(+)/PD-1(+), indicating patients with anti-PD1 positive could have a stronger immunotherapy response (p < 0.001; Fig. 9F).

div.head: Discussion
div.p: Herein, STEAP3 was elevated in numerous solid tumors, in line with our findings from the IHC, TCGA, and GSE108474 cohorts. Additionally, elevated STEAP3 expression levels were linked to shorter overall survival times for glioma patients. Subgroup studies in TCGA and the validation dataset showed a relationship between STEAP3 expression and poorer outcomes in patients with GB. Noteworthily, univariate and multivariate Cox regression analyses identified STEAP3 as an independent glioma prognostic marker. In the current study, survival analysis across different glioma subtypes also highlighted the high predictive value of STEAP3 for IDHmutants and 1p/19q codeleted astrocytomas, whereas its prognostic value was restricted or unclear in other glioma subtypes. us, STEAP3-targeting treatment has been proposed to improve response in patients with astrocytomas and IDH mutations and 1p/19q codeletion.

Patients with high levels of STEAP3 had low overall survival times, according to the KM survival analysis. STEAP3 was predominantly abundant in the cytoplasm and membrane of specimens in the HPA database, with significantly higher expression levels observed in tumor tissues. It is worthwhile emphasizing that STEAP3 protein levels were higher in GB tissues compared to non-malignant brain tissues. e aforementioned conclusions were validated in the training cohort and validation set. According to the CancerSEA single-cell database, STEAP3 might be associated with poor overall survival. An earlier study hypothesized that 26 STEAP3 is implicated in the EMT of gliomas, and its knockdown may inhibit the migratory and invasive capabilities of T98G cells. IHC staining corroborated the stability and dependability of this prognostic marker. Darker staining represents higher STEAP3 expression levels, which promotes tumor progression and a poor prognosis. Taken together, our results collectively suggest that STEAP3 may be a valuable prognostic biomarker for GB.

STEAP3-related genes were principally implicated in leukocyte migration, collagen-containing extracellular matrix, TNF signaling pathway, receptor-ligand activity, cytokine-cytokine receptor interaction, and JAK-STAT signaling pathway, according to the GO and KEGG enrichment analyses. A study reported that STEAP3 stimulates cell division, growth, and proliferation 7 . Upregulating STEAP3 expression activates the STAT3-FoxM1 pathway and up-regulates the expression of transferrin receptors, which in turn leads to more aggressive glioma cell morphologies 31 . JAK2/STAT3 inhibition has been shown to suppress the formation of the mesenchymal chemoresistant subgroup 32 . rough a number of pathways, the JAK/STAT system may partially promote STEAP3 phosphorylation, inflammation, and progression 33 . As previously mentioned, STEAP3 might be crucial to the carcinogenesis of GB. Studies have described that suppressing the expression of SLC7A11 enhanced ferroptosis, which was achieved through the activation of the JAK/STAT pathway in adrenocortical carcinoma cells 34 . Some studies found that STEAP3 knockdown induced ferroptosis in ovarian cancer cells via the regulation of SLC7A11 34 . Meanwhile, the JAK/STAT pathway plays an instrumental role in glioblastoma progression 35 . Consequently, our findings conjointly implied that STEAP3 may mediate the JAK-STAT signaling pathway to influence the invasion and proliferation of GB cells. Analysis of the TME revealed a link between STEAP3 expression, immunological checkpoints, and tumorinfiltrating immune cells, which play prognostic roles in gliomas 36,37 . Patients with higher expression levels of STEAP3 derive more benefits from immunotherapy, as evidenced by the increased IPS and TIDE scores. Consequently, STEAP3 may be a useful predictor of immunotherapy responses in GB patients. Nevertheless, further comprehensive research is warranted to elucidate the precise mechanisms of interaction between STEAP3, tumor-infiltrating immune cells in the TME, and immunological checkpoints. Fortunately, previous study has demonstrated that a favorable prognosis for GB is predicted by low 2 balance and low PD-L1/PD-1 axis activity 38 . Furthermore, our results also showed that STEAP3 is related to T cell status, such as helper T cells and Tregs, and immune checkpoint mechanisms including CTLA-4 and PD-1/PD-L1 immune tolerance.

eir research results provide a theoretical basis for our further research 38 . e ImmuneScore, ESTIMATEScore, and StromalScore significantly varied between the high and low STEAP3 expression groups. Numerous studies focusing on cancer have established the significance of StromalScore in tumor growth, metastasis, and treatment resistance 25,26 . According to our estimation approach, there might be a connection between the STEAP3 expression and the development and metastasis of GB.

Nevertheless, this study has several limitations that merit acknowledgment. To begin, batch effects could not be fully eliminated during cohort validation. Furthermore, this was a retrospective cohort study that could not establish causality. erefore, follow-up research is necessitated to validate our findings.

div.head: Conclusion
div.p: Herein, the expression level of STEAP3 was significantly higher in tumor tissues compared to non-malignant brain tissues. Higher STEAP3 expression levels were associated with a poor prognosis in GB patients. Additionally, STEAP3 may potentially modulate GB cell growth and metastasis. STEAP3 expression was also significantly correlated with IPS, immunological checkpoints, and tumor-infiltrating immune cells. Taken these findings suggest that STEAP3 may be a promising therapeutic target as well as an independent predictive biomarker for guiding treatment strategies in GB patients.
